name: Easy Tracker
pitchShort: Share your live location with one link. The person you send it to sees you coming on a map, with no app or account. Sharing ends when you tap Stop or after 12 hours.
descriptionLong:
Easy Tracker is an Android app for the trip over. Open it and your live location link is already on the screen: copy it and send it to whoever is waiting for you.

They open the link in their phone's browser and see where you are on a live map. They don't need the app or an account, and the map can estimate distance and a rough arrival time on their own phone.

Privacy is built in: only your latest point is shared, no location history is kept, and nothing is sold. Sharing stops when you tap Stop, or automatically after 12 hours, and the old link stops working. On Android a notification stays visible while sharing is on.

Easy Tracker is in testing / development and is not in the app stores yet. You can download the free Android test build (APK) from the download page, which has install steps.

name: CyberArena 3D
pitchShort: A neon first-person arena shooter that runs in your browser. Pick a callsign and armor colour, then fight AI practice bots with a live scoreboard and kill feed. Free, no install.
descriptionLong:
CyberArena 3D is a free first-person shooter built with Three.js that runs right in the browser, with no download or account.

Choose a callsign and an armor colour, deploy into a neon cyber arena and fight three AI practice bots. Move with W, A, S, D, aim with the mouse, click to fire your laser rifle and press Space to jump. On phones and tablets there is an on-screen joystick, a look area, and fire and jump buttons.

The HUD shows your health, kills, deaths and streak, plus a live scoreboard and kill feed. When you are eliminated you respawn after a short countdown.

CyberArena is in testing / development. Right now it runs in single-player Local Arena mode against bots; online multiplayer is planned but not switched on yet.

name: Ollama
pitchShort: Run open large language models such as Llama, Gemma, Qwen and DeepSeek on your own Mac, Windows or Linux machine with one command.
descriptionLong:
Ollama is a free, open-source (MIT) tool for running large language models locally. Pull a model with one command and chat with it in the terminal, or call it from your own apps through a local REST API that is also compatible with the OpenAI API format.

It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, uses your GPU when available, and keeps your prompts on your own machine. A large library of open models is available, and you can build custom models with a Modelfile.

Source code: https://github.com/ollama/ollama

name: Open WebUI
pitchShort: A self-hosted, ChatGPT-style web interface for local and cloud AI models, with chat history, document RAG, users and plugins.
descriptionLong:
Open WebUI is a feature-rich, self-hosted AI chat interface that works offline. Connect it to Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API and get a polished web app with conversations, model switching, document upload and retrieval (RAG), web search, multi-user accounts with roles, and an extension system for tools and functions.

It installs with Docker or pip. The source is on GitHub (https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) under the Open WebUI License, a BSD-3-based licence that adds a branding-preservation clause for larger deployments; check it if you plan to rebrand.

Free to self-host.

name: Excalidraw
pitchShort: A virtual whiteboard for sketching hand-drawn-style diagrams, wireframes and flowcharts, with live collaboration and end-to-end encryption.
descriptionLong:
Excalidraw is a free, open-source (MIT) virtual whiteboard. It gives diagrams and wireframes a friendly hand-drawn look, works in the browser with no sign-up, and supports real-time collaboration with end-to-end encrypted sharing links.

Drawings can be exported to PNG, SVG or the open .excalidraw format, and developers can embed the editor in their own apps with the @excalidraw/excalidraw React package. A paid Excalidraw+ plan exists for teams, but the editor itself is free and open source.

Source code: https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw

name: n8n
pitchShort: A visual workflow automation tool with 400+ integrations and AI agent nodes. Fair-code: free to self-host, source-available under the Sustainable Use License.
descriptionLong:
n8n lets you build automations by connecting nodes on a canvas: triggers, hundreds of app integrations, code steps in JavaScript or Python, and AI nodes for building LLM agents and RAG pipelines.

About the licence, honestly: n8n is fair-code, not OSI open source. The source is public on GitHub (https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n) under the Sustainable Use License, which lets you self-host and use it for free for your own internal business purposes, but restricts reselling it as a hosted service. Some enterprise features use a separate licence, and n8n also sells a paid cloud plan.

The self-hosted Community Edition is free.

name: Godot Engine
pitchShort: A free, MIT-licensed 2D and 3D game engine with its own editor, GDScript and C# support, and exports to desktop, mobile and the web.
descriptionLong:
Godot is a complete, cross-platform game engine for 2D and 3D games. It ships as a small download with a full editor, a scene and node system, the Python-like GDScript language plus C# and C++ (GDExtension) support, physics, animation, UI and shader tools.

Games can be exported to Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and the web. Godot is released under the MIT licence with no royalties or fees, and is developed by a community supported by the non-profit Godot Foundation.

Source code: https://github.com/godotengine/godot

name: Blender
pitchShort: The free, open-source 3D creation suite: modelling, sculpting, animation, rendering, compositing, video editing and 2D animation in one app.
descriptionLong:
Blender covers the whole 3D pipeline: modelling, sculpting, UV and texturing, rigging and animation, simulation, the Cycles and EEVEE renderers, compositing, motion tracking, video editing and Grease Pencil 2D animation.

It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, is scriptable with Python, and is released under the GNU GPL. Development is led by the Blender Foundation and Blender Institute and funded by the community through the Blender Development Fund.

Source code: https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender

name: Coolify
pitchShort: An open-source, self-hostable alternative to Heroku, Netlify and Vercel: deploy apps, databases and 280+ one-click services to your own servers.
descriptionLong:
Coolify turns your own VPS or bare-metal servers into a platform-as-a-service. Connect a Git repository and it builds and deploys your app (Dockerfile, Nixpacks or Docker Compose), with automatic SSL, preview deployments, databases with backups, and a catalogue of one-click services.

Coolify is open source under the Apache 2.0 licence and free to self-host on as many servers as you like, with no vendor lock-in. A paid Coolify Cloud plan is available if you would rather not host the dashboard yourself.

Source code: https://github.com/coollabsio/coolify
